headline: Single-cell and regulatory profiling map disease-linked cell states across tissues
label: Cell Type Genomics Of Disease
summary: Disease and aging variation is increasingly resolved at cell-state and regulatory resolution, from pancreatic beta cells to autism lncRNA networks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving disease- and aging-associated programs at single-cell resolution and linking them to regulatory context. A manifold-based unsupervised metric quantifies transcriptional dyscoordination that tracks aging, senescence and T-cell expansion. In human pancreas, harmonization of 18 public scRNA-seq datasets into a 266,000-cell atlas infers three beta-cell stress trajectories across aging and diabetes. In autism spectrum disorder, the Clean hidden-causality method infers dynamic lncRNA regulatory networks. MoDIFI integrates RNA-seq, ATAC-seq and Hi-C in a Bayesian framework to prioritize neuronal cell lines and regulatory regions for neurodevelopmental variants. Complementary resources cover basal ganglia multi-omics across four species and single-cell proteomics of the developing human brain. What is new here is the move from cell-type labels toward quantitative state trajectories and regulatory inference, although the items differ in modality and scope.
